name: practice_line
about: practice-line — a line to follow, and something to stop at.
A 2.0 × 1.0 m white floor with a 20 mm dark line running along +X
from the spawn point, and a stop bar across it at +X 1.2 m.
The line is deliberately the same width as the sensor separation
the chassis carries (the two downward cameras sit ±18 mm off
centre), so a centred robot has BOTH sensors on the mat either
side of the line and reads a near-zero error — which is what a
differential line-follower steers on. Drift either way and the
inboard sensor crosses onto the line, producing a large,
correctly-signed error.
The stop bar is the intersection case: wide enough that both
sensors go dark at once, which is what ``line_follow.py`` treats
as "stop" rather than "steer". A branch that darkens only ONE
sensor must be ignored, so a short stub is included at +X 0.6 m
to exercise exactly that.
Geometry is slabs rather than a texture on purpose: the colour
sensor resolves an untextured geom from its rgba, so this world
needs no PNG and stays byte-identical across platforms — a
control test that fails should mean the control law changed, not
that an image decoded differently.
Origin at floor centre-left. +X forward of the spawned chassis.
All dimensions in metres.

geoms.name: floor
note: White floor — 2.0 × 1.0 m, from 0.5 m behind the spawn to
1.5 m ahead: the line (to x = 1.3) and the stop bar (x = 1.2)
must lie ON it. Centred on the origin it ended at x = 1.0,
and a sensor past that edge read "dark" (nothing to reflect
off) — a false intersection 20 cm short of the bar.

geoms.name: line_branch
note: Branch stub: darkens the LEFT sensor only. A follower that
steers toward a single dark sensor peels off onto this; the
correct behaviour is to hold course until it passes.
